answer: Agents bidding on orchard and garden irrigation jobs must solve a memory-hard puzzle seeded by a public beacon, their key and the epoch. Validators recompute a compact proof and reject a wrong result or reused admission. A new key changes the puzzle, so one solution cannot admit many aliases. Each extra identity buys another allocation of memory and computation; parallel rigs reduce delay but still pay the aggregate cost. This assumes the puzzle has no shortcut and admission cost exceeds the gain from one extra seat; cheap hardware weakens the deterrent.
